title: answers.json: lt-module-answer → lt-module-fill / mechanistic-diagram / lt-module-export
description: Drafted answers with per-segment provenance. Represent each draft as segments so every sentence is structurally traceable to a tag.

schema_version.description: Version 2 adds label_placements and requires it for drafted image-labeling, drag-and-drop-labeling and categorization items. Version 1 remains valid and readable so older drafts can be re-exported. Emit 2 on every new draft.

source_module.description: Binds the draft to an exact capture. `sha256` identifies the capture. `question_digest` establishes whether its questions remain unchanged. A re-capture that changes questions invalidates the draft. Recording only the student's answers does not.

path.description: The capture this draft answers. A relative path resolves against this answers file's own folder. The validator checks the binding only when the path resolves to a file.

question_digest.description: sha256 of the questions alone, as ltcore.digest defines them: ids, types, prompts, options and the authored constraints, kept in page order (python3 -m ltcore.digest --view <module.json> prints the hashed view). Optional so older drafts stay valid; write it on every new draft. Without it the validator enforces `sha256` strictly, and a post-fill re-capture fails although no question changed. Media, target_geometry, constraints.note and all state fields are left out: a change there still moves `sha256`, which is then reported as a note while question_digest holds.

tier1_corpus.description: Tier-1 material consulted for this module: lecture ids, transcript paths and ILO sections. An empty list requires a tier_descent record of 'absent'.

status.description: blocked = a TODO, which counts as a successful handoff. skipped = standing policy, e.g. an iRAT page.

skip_reason.description: Required when status is 'skipped'. Include every skipped item and its reason in the review packet to prevent silent omissions. 'already-answered' and 'course-feedback' record those skips. 'irat-policy' and 'trat-answers-unavailable' distinguish permanently excluded closed-book work from a tRAT awaiting an answers file. See docs/design-notes.md for applicable policies. 'read-only-mirror' records a panel flagged by item.mirror_of. Such panels accept no writes and may appear empty, so 'already-answered' does not describe them. Drafting their cells wastes answer content.

segments.description: The draft, in order. Render concatenated for the packet; render with tags inline for audit.

kind.description: claim = carries factual content and REQUIRES >=1 provenance_ref. connective = pure linking prose, no factual content, capped at 120 chars per segment and 25% of the answer by the validator. Those caps are a tripwire against relabelling claims as prose, not a proof of tagging: no validator can tell the two apart, so the packet renders connective segments distinctly for the human.

ref.description: Local id referenced by segments, e.g. 'p1'.

source_id.description: Tier 4 MUST be a resolvable DOI (10.x/…) or PMID:<digits>. An unresolvable identifier is a fabrication and is deleted, not softened.

tag.description: Rendered provenance tag, e.g. [T1:lecture-1:slide-14]. Derived from the authoritative structured fields.

tier_descent.description: Record a reason for descending each tier. Reaching tier 3 requires accounts of tiers 1 and 2. Validated for completeness.

uncertainties.description: State each uncertainty as a question without smoothing it over. 'low' confidence requires at least one.

conflicts.description: Surface conflicts without silently reconciling them. Renders as ⚠ Conflict in the export.

diagram_brief.description: Handed to mechanistic-diagram together with the item's target_geometry from module.json.

role.description: SBGN Activity Flow semantics using the suite's glyphs.

asset_captions.description: Caption per asset_refs entry, keyed by the entry as written. Write the caption here when an Lt figure attached to the relevant item lacks alt text in the capture.

single_attempt_approval.description: Records approval to type this single-attempt item's draft into Lt. Store the approval in <data>/runs/<module_id>/approvals.json with an approval_id matching ^A-[0-9a-f]{8}$. emit_fill.py requires approval for single-attempt items and rejects it on items the capture does not mark single-attempt. Approval covers only writing through the model. Fill scripts never click Submit or Check Answer. The human submits.

approval_id.description: The approval_id identifying the user's approval in <data>/runs/<module_id>/approvals.json. Format: A- plus 8 hexadecimal characters, matching ^A-[0-9a-f]{8}$. emit_fill.py checks that the approval exists.

proposed_selection.description: For multiple-choice, option_ids supported by reasoning in segments. Reading panelState.modelAnswer is permitted and on by default. `model_answer.read` (default true) can disable it. Drafted selections still require reasoning and provenance tags. Copying the key would evaluate the suite against the key instead of its research.

label_placements.description: Required in schema_version 2 for drafted image-labeling, drag-and-drop-labeling and categorization items. Records where each label goes, as table_cells records grid answers. Describe the target in prose. Capture emits no anchor coordinates, and option_id refers to a position in an alphabetically sorted pool. Describe anchors so a fill run can resolve them against the picture.

label.description: Label text verbatim from the item's options[].text. The cross-check rejects other text to prevent invented vocabulary.

target.description: Where the label goes. For the two labelling types, describe an anchor so a human or fill run can find it, e.g. 'the upper-left circle'. For categorization, use the bin title verbatim from constraints.categories. There is no category_titles field.

target_index.description: Only where the index is genuinely knowable from the capture - a categorization bin's position in constraints.categories, which is emitted in the order the student sees it and is therefore knowable. NEVER guess one for an image anchor.

confidence.description: Confidence per placement. medium or low requires `alternative`, enforced by the validator (ltcore.validate). See docs/design-notes.md for confidence limits.

alternative.description: The competing reading: the structure this label might sit on instead. Named, not gestured at.

table_cells.description: For table-completion: one entry per cell to be written.

todo.description: A clear TODO counts as a successful handoff. Required when status is 'blocked'.
